connector: The ransom note is written. Now someone has to carry it to the castle, and nobody wants that job. Today the outlaws argue, Jemmy bosses them like a prince, and the real prince makes a choice that leaves Jemmy struck dumb.

vcloze2.h1: The boy refuses boldly. Which bank word means boldly refusing to obey?
vcloze2.why: defiant means boldly refusing to obey.

vcloze3.h1: It is a private talk to work something out. Which bank word means that?
vcloze3.why: a parley is a talk between two sides.

match.mulishness: Mulishness has the word mule in it. Look for the stubborn meaning.
match.defiant: Defiant means standing up and saying no. Look for the meaning about boldly refusing.
match.parley: A parley is a kind of talk. Look for the meaning about a conversation.
match.contrary: Contrary means doing the opposite. Look for that meaning.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
money that kidnappers ask for before they let someone go
a sentence made of two complete thoughts joined by a word like and, but, or so
a group of words that makes sense on its own, like The outlaw growled.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. The ransom note is written. Now somebody has to carry it to the castle, and nobody wants that job. These two chapters are loud. People shout and stomp, and one boy makes a choice that leaves Jemmy speechless. As you read, ask yourself: why would he choose that?
transcripts.guide1: Word work. You’ll build words that share the root that means carry, and you’ll find where the comma goes in a compound sentence. Here’s the trick: the comma sits right in front of the joining word, like a little doorstop. Then you’ll snap word parts together, one tile at a time.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: Chapter 10 is a battle of words. Jemmy uses big, bossy prince talk on the outlaws. Listen to how they react. In Chapter 11, the prince gets a chance most kids would grab. Watch what he does with it, and watch Jemmy’s face.
transcripts.guide3: Every paragraph needs a good ending. A conclusion is your last word, the sentence a reader carries away. Don’t just copy your first sentence. Say your big idea in a fresh way, and make it sound finished, like closing a door.

notes.wordParts: The root port means “carry.” transport = carry across, import = carry in, export = carry out, report = carry back, portable = able to be carried.
notes.grammar: A compound sentence joins two complete thoughts with a comma and a joining word: Jemmy wrote the note, and Billy watched.
notes.spelling: When a word ends in a consonant + le, that consonant goes with the le to make the last syllable: ta·ble, can·dle, sim·ple.
notes.wgrd: Good readers notice when a character changes, even a little, and they ask why.
vocab: stubborn refusal to obey; acting like a mule
a private talk between two sides, often enemies
always doing the opposite; hard to deal with

Think about the prince today. He gets a chance to go home, and he says no. Jemmy can't understand it. Is the prince just being a brat again? Or is something else going on inside him? Watch closely. Sometimes people do things for reasons they don't say out loud.

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 10–11 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapters 10 and 11 in your book. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. Remember, the outlaws think the real prince is the whipping boy! In Chapter 10, they decide to send him to the castle with the note. Watch what the prince says. In Chapter 11, Billy pulls off his belt. Watch what Jemmy does. Stop at each question, think of your answer, and keep reading. After you read, do the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now answer in full sentences, with details from the book. One, Chapter 11 asks if the prince has sand for brains. What does the prince do that makes Jemmy think that? Two, why might the prince not want to go home? Look at what he says about his father. Three, when the outlaws step outside, what do Jemmy and the prince argue about, and what does the prince decide? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Write one conclusion sentence. Say your big idea in a new way.
mods.script: Every opinion needs an ending. It's called a conclusion. A good conclusion doesn't just repeat your first sentence. It says your big idea in a fresh way, and it gives your reader something to think about. Listen to the end of Clara's: A true prince would learn to use his power to protect, not to punish. Doesn't that sound like an ending? Now write a conclusion sentence for your own paragraph. Don't copy your first sentence word for word.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: The prince tosses away his herring and shows no care for what happens to Jemmy.
items.why: Not caring about someone in danger is not courage.

items.t: Jemmy keeps up his trick so the outlaws will send the prince home.
items.why: He could be caught any minute, but he keeps trying to help.

items.t: Billy grabs his belt to whip the prince. Jemmy speaks up with a new idea: send the horse.
items.why: He speaks up to two angry outlaws to stop a whipping. That takes courage.
